subject: Change order: scope rebalance & fee offset for PilotHealth
messages:
From: Sara Wong <sara.wong@pilothealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts <contracts@pilothealth.com>, procurement@pilothealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: PilotHealth request: scope rebalance + one-time fee offset

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at PilotHealth is moving ahead with phase 2 but we need to reallocate some of our committed nodes. We have two asks: 

1) Move 30% of our original Dedicated GPU commitment from the inference-heavy pipeline to the vector-search workload (same region).
2) Because the reallocation shortens our original implementation schedule, we are asking for a one-time pro-rata fee offset to cover onboarding costs.

We'd like to capture this in a short change order rather than re-signing the order form. Can you share a draft CO (scope + effective dates + net fee impact)? Contracts here (cc) will need the redline.

Target timeline: implementation week of Nov 15; legal hopes to finish redlines by Nov 9.

Attachment: PilotHealth_OrderForm_v3.pdf (application/pdf)

Thanks,
Sara Wong
Head of Platform Partnerships
PilotHealth

--

> [original internal note — copied for context]
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Wong <sara.wong@pilothealth.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Contracts <contracts@pilothealth.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PilotHealth request: scope rebalance + one-time fee offset

Sara — thanks for the clear asks. I put together a short change order template and a proposed commercial treatment for the one-time pro-rata offset. Key points: 

- Scope: reassign 30% of committed nodes from Inference Tier B (model serving) to Vector Indexing Tier A (embedding + kNN), same billing band. Effective Nov 15, 2027.
- Fees: no increase to committed throughput; one-time credit equal to 25% of the implementation fee for the replaced capacity, applied to the next invoice.
- Term & acceptance: CO modifies Exhibit A of the Order Form; signature by both parties required.

Draft attached: PH_change_order_draft_redlines.docx 
Can Connor and legal (laura) take a first pass on legal language today/tomorrow? We need to close redlines by Nov 9 to meet their timeline.

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal redline (Redwood) — due Nov 4
2) Counter-redline (PilotHealth) — due Nov 7
3) Final sign & implementation kickoff — target Nov 15

Thanks — I can hop on a quick call if helpful.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Executive
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attachment: PH_change_order_draft_redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Contracts <contracts@pilothealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 14:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: PilotHealth request: scope rebalance + one-time fee offset — legal redlines

Rishi / team —

I've reviewed the draft CO and added tracked redlines in the attached. High-level comments: 

- Please confirm whether the "same billing band" language means we keep the existing SKU unit price. If PilotHealth's Vector Indexing usage has materially different performance characteristics we should add a clause that preserves per-token/per-embedding unit accounting.
- Add explicit SLA carryover language: any change to capacity must preserve the original SLA commitments for latency and availability for the workloads that move. If PilotHealth requires a different latency SLO for Vector Indexing we need to treat that as a scope change and price accordingly.
- The one-time credit should be described as a "bill credit" to avoid confusion with recurring discounts. Include an invoice reference and expiration for use (suggest 90 days).
- We should include a short rollback clause: if the implementation requires >3 weeks of configuration/engineering beyond the baseline plan, each party will negotiate a good-faith amendment to fees and timeline.

I've attached laura_CO_redlines.docx with inline comments. I also flagged a data residency paragraph — Connor, confirm that moving nodes within the same region preserves the customer's existing data residency obligations (I believe yes).

Timeline: if we turn this around today we can be ready for PilotHealth counter-redline by Nov 7.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: laura_CO_redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)

Subject: Re: PilotHealth request: scope rebalance + one-time fee offset — approval & execution path

Team — good work closing this quickly. A couple of operational notes and approvals from my side: 

1) I approve the one-time pro-rata bill credit as described by Laura (25% of the affected implementation fee, applied as a bill credit with 90-day expiration). Given the customer relationship and likelihood of expansion on Dedicated, this is acceptable.
2) Ops: Connor, please confirm there are no infra-side blockers for the Nov 15 swap and prepare a short migration runbook (rollback steps + smoke tests).
3) Finance: I gave verbal approval to apply the credit, but please route for a Finance sign-off on the credit memo and confirm accounting codes before execution.
4) Execution: Rishi, please send the final DocuSign packet to PilotHealth when legal confirms we incorporated SLA carryover and the rollback clause. Link below for the DocuSign template; use DEAL-4839 as the reference.

DocuSign (template prepared): https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC123-PilotHealth-CO
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/4839

Marissa Cole
